theory: A slinky carrying a current $I$ is a solenoid whose turns per metre change as it is stretched. Inside a long solenoid of $N$ turns and length $L$ the field is uniform:
At constant current a graph of $B$ against $N/L$ is a straight line through the origin with slope $\mu_0 I$, so $\mu_0 = \dfrac{\text{slope}}{I}$.
For a slinky that is not much longer than its diameter $D$, the field at the centre is smaller: $B = \mu_0 N I / \sqrt{L^{2} + D^{2}}$. Short lengths fall below the line.
A Hall probe also reads Earth's field and its own offset, so it must be zeroed at the centre of the slinky with the current switched off.

apparatus.slinky: Slinky spring: a long, open coil of N turns.
apparatus.supply: DC power supply with a rheostat to set the current.
apparatus.ammeter: Ammeter in series with the slinky.
apparatus.probe: Hall probe and teslameter, reading to 0.001 mT.
apparatus.rule: Metre rule (1.5 m) along the bench, with clamps to hold the slinky's ends.

safety: Keep the current below about 3 A: the slinky warms up at high currents.
Switch the supply off while you re-clamp the slinky.
steps: With the supply off, put the Hall probe at the centre of the slinky and zero the teslameter.
Switch on and set a steady current with the rheostat. Record N and I.
Stretch the slinky to a length L and read L on the metre rule.
Read B on the teslameter with the probe at the centre.
Repeat for at least six lengths, keeping I constant (check the ammeter each time).
Work out N/L and plot B against N/L.
tips: Zero with the current OFF: zeroing with it on removes the very field you want to measure.
Keep the turns evenly spaced along the slinky before each reading.
Read the slinky's end square-on to the rule (Eye level view).
references: Young, H. D. & Freedman, R. A. University Physics, ch. 28: Sources of magnetic field (field of a solenoid).
Physics Bench virtual laboratory — slinky practical.

notZeroed.title: The teslameter was not zeroed before your readings
notZeroed.detail: Earth's field and the probe's offset add to every reading, giving an intercept and a biased slope. Zero it at the centre of the slinky with the current off.

zeroedWithCurrent.title: The teslameter was zeroed with the current on
zeroedWithCurrent.detail: Zeroing with the current flowing subtracts the slinky's own field from every later reading. Switch the supply off, zero, then switch on again.

currentChanged.title: The current was changed during your readings
currentChanged.detail: B ∝ (N/L)·I only gives a straight line if I stays the same. Keep the rheostat fixed and check the ammeter at each length.

endEffects.title: Short lengths fall below the line
endEffects.detail: When L is not much bigger than the slinky's diameter the field at the centre is less than μ₀NI/L. Mention this end effect in your discussion, or leave those points out of your line.
